triage.note: The counterpart PR #21 R1/R2/R3 established: a check that asserts the real file is clean also passes vacuously once it regresses, so a known-bad fixture has to prove the miss is actually caught. Eight mutations, eleven failures, exact count — the checkbox carries two independent defects (`checked` and `disabled`) on one element — `min_failures` alone is a floor and would let a regressed check that ALSO over-fires report green (PR #21 round-2 R5). The shapes are listed in the fixture's own header comment; the two that matter most are the checked-and-disabled checkbox (a paid tier as the deployed default, on a control nobody can untick) and a `routingStrip` that is declared, is never called from the banner, and prints no cost — the demo's own failure shape, a number computed and not shown, moved one layer up. PR #58 R6 added shape 7 and three of the ten: a page that offers the escalate box unconditionally — never asking the server whether it is armed, never disabling the control, never rendering the server's refusal — is a tickable box whose value is silently discarded on an unarmed deployment. With a real credential about to land on a public, unauthenticated host, that is the shape most worth catching. PR #58 R17/R19 added shape 8 and the eleventh: a strip with no truncation clause at all. Its predecessor clause was worse than absent — it said 'the first N chars' about rung 1's window, which starts at the largest unattributed region and on 18 of 43 dev documents does not start at 0, so the screen stated a falsehood the envelope could not even contradict (no offset was published). The pin therefore requires the RANGE, read from the record's own `offset`, not a length. **RE-PINNED 2026-08-27** on the owner's "make it default on, remove the button". Count unchanged at 11 and the two families are re-derived, not re-counted. Four of the previous eight shapes pinned a checkbox that no longer exists (`checked`, `disabled`, the dropped upload flag, and the unconditional box that never asked whether the server was armed) — none is a defect the page can still have. They are replaced by ONE shape of the opposite polarity: the removed control creeping back whole — a `#escalate` box, an `escalateOn()` helper, the flag on the fixture wire and on the upload query string, the arming round-trip, and the `escalation_disarmed` note — six failures, one per absent-pin. The last of the six is worse than useless rather than merely wrong: the server no longer emits `escalation_disarmed`, so a page rendering it carries an honesty mechanism that can never fire. The five display failures (banner never calls the strip, no cost, no truncation clause, pane drops the deterministic evidence and the tier that replaced it) are unchanged.

provenance: D11, created 2026-08-26 alongside the check it falsifies, per hard rule 2. Extended 2026-08-27 in the PR #58 round-1 repair with the arming shape; count 7 -> 10. Extended 2026-08-27 (PR #58 round 3) with the truncation-clause shape; count 10 -> 11. Re-derived 2026-08-27 on the owner's control removal; count 11 -> 11, with four checkbox shapes replaced by one control-creep shape worth six.
